newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sets prices on Japanese, Korean D-RAM chips.
newsitem.headline: EU sets prices on Japanese, Korean D-RAM chips.

text.p: The European Commission said on Monday it was reintroducing minimum prices on D-RAM computer chips originating in Japan and Korea with immediate effect.
The EU imposed anti-dumping duties on Japanese exporters in January 1990 and later on Korean exporters. The measures were suspended 21 months ago due to the rise in D-RAM prices.
It said the minimum prices would be introduced gradually to avoid harming the EU chip market where prices for D-RAMs are currently low.
There will be no immediate increase in D-RAM prices on Monday, officials said, adding that the first date when measures might affect prices would be April 1.

Officials would not say what those prices would be, although they said they had told the relevant companies, an approach they said was to preserve the commercial confidentiality of information supplied to the Commission inquiry.
The EU market for D-RAM chips -- which stands for dynamic random access chip -- was worth five billion European currency units ($5.7 billion) in 1995, a Commission official told reporters.
Measures are intended to protect EU producers of D-RAMs which include Motorola, Siemens and Texas Instruments, the officials said.
The spokesman said 12 Japanese and three Korean companies were involved but he declined to give any names -- Brussels Newsroom 32 2 287 6800
